The product

Hand it the paperwork.Get your day back.

BlueSpark™ automates your daily work on the computer you already have, without changing the systems you use.

Join the Founding 500Book a consultation

A day with BlueSpark™

From morning to night

  1. Morning.

    You drop a folder of invoices, contracts and emails into BlueSpark™. It reads every page and remembers what matters.

  2. Midday.

    It works through the pile on its own: matching invoices, flagging a clause that changed, preparing the summary you need. Every number it shows you comes from your own files.

  3. When something’s off.

    It doesn’t guess. It tells you exactly what it couldn’t confirm, so you decide.

  4. Night.

    While you sleep, BlueSpark™ reviews the day and learns how you like things done. Tomorrow, it’s a little better at your job.

How it’s built

An AI built like a brain.

Other AIs are a model with features. BlueSpark™ is an organism with a model inside.

01

It remembers.

BlueSpark™ has a neuromorphic brain, a memory that works the way yours does. Important things get stronger every time you use them. Clutter fades away. Close your laptop on Friday, open it on Monday, and it knows exactly where you left off.

02

It thinks about its own thinking.

BlueSpark™ is the first AI with metacognition. Before it acts, it asks itself: am I sure? If it isn’t, it tests its ideas, checks the facts, and tells you plainly.

03

It sleeps.

Every night, BlueSpark™ goes over the day’s work, keeps the lessons that proved true, and files away the mistakes so it never repeats them.

It grows with you.

The longer you use it, the better it gets at your job. Its intelligence comes from your work, not from someone else’s data.

Why it’s different

Four differences you can see.

Most AI tools are a chatbot in a web browser. When a file is missing or a folder changes, they have no idea what went wrong. BlueSpark™ is built like a careful, curious coworker: it investigates before it touches anything.

01

The broken robot vs. the curious colleague

Standard AI runs in blind loops. When something goes wrong, it repeats the same broken action again and again. BlueSpark™ finds out why the file was missing and fixes the path before it acts.

Blind loop: repeats and crashesCuriosity: investigates and solves
02

Monday amnesia vs. a good night’s sleep

Chatbots wipe their memory the second you close the tab. BlueSpark™ keeps a continuous memory on your PC, and a quiet nightly clean-up files the day’s notes into lasting know-how.

Chatbot: amnesia every morningSleep: notes filed into neat drawers
03

Faking “done” vs. the double-check

Standard AI says “I saved your report” because it predicted polite words. BlueSpark™ has a strict double-check habit: it verifies the real file on your hard drive first.

Faking: says saved, file missingChecked: verified on the hard drive
04

Sending files away vs. staying on your desk

Standard AI uploads your contracts and financials to cloud servers where they can be logged or leaked. With BlueSpark™, your documents stay on your own laptop.

Public cloud: files exposedPrivate laptop: stays on your desk

What it remembers

A memory like a nervous system, not a notebook.

Five layers, from what is in play right now down to how you like to work. What you use gets stronger, what you ignore fades, and overnight the day settles into lasting knowledge. None of this is a new idea. It is how human memory has been understood for well over a century, and it all lives on your own computer.

Five layers, one place.

Everything lives in one place on your computer, so there is one version of the truth.

  1. Working
    what is in play right now
  2. Episodic
    what happened, and when
  3. Semantic
    facts, and how they connect
  4. Procedural
    how you usually get things done
  5. Persona
    how you like to work
↑ Used: gets stronger↓ Ignored: fades☾ Overnight: settles into knowledge

What science found, and where it shows up.

A hundred and forty years of memory research, from the first experiments to the sleeping brain.

  1. 1885Hermann Ebbinghaus

    Memory fades fast unless it is revisited, and every repeat slows the fading.

    Ignored memories fade
  2. 1894Santiago Ramón y Cajal

    Memories may form by strengthening the connections between brain cells that already exist.

    Used memories get stronger
  3. 1900Georg Müller & Alfons Pilzecker

    New learning is not permanent at once. It needs time to settle.

    Overnight settling
  4. 1949Donald Hebb

    Connections that are used together grow stronger together.

    Used memories get stronger
  5. 1957Brenda Milner & William Scoville

    The famous patient H.M. could no longer form new memories of events, yet could still learn a skill. Remembering what happened and knowing how to do something are separate.

    Episodic and Procedural layers
  6. 1972Endel Tulving

    Remembering events and knowing facts are two different kinds of memory.

    Episodic and Semantic layers
  7. 1974Alan Baddeley & Graham Hitch

    We hold what we are working on in a small mental workspace.

    Working layer
  8. 1994Matthew Wilson & Bruce McNaughton

    Brain cells in sleeping rats replayed the patterns from the day. Sleep is when experience is sorted and kept.

    Overnight settling

Your brain doesn’t keep every random email. At night it sweeps away the trivial chatter and files what matters. BlueSpark™ does the same on your laptop, so Monday morning feels like coming back to a colleague who was there on Friday.

Skills are earned, not assumed.

BlueSpark™ notices patterns in how you work and suggests routines. A suggestion only becomes a skill after it passes checks, and a skill that starts failing goes back to being a suggestion. You can hand-craft skills too. They go through the same checks.

Mahanta OS

Three technologies. One operating system.

Each of these ideas has decades of research behind it. None of them is new on its own. What makes BlueSpark™ different is that they work together, as one.

Brain-inspired memory

The neuromorphic brain

Where it comes from: neuromorphic engineering, the field that asks what computers can learn from the way nervous systems are built. It was pioneered by Carver Mead at Caltech in the 1980s.

Thinking it through

First-principles reasoning

Where it comes from: the habit of working things out from the ground up, instead of repeating what was done before. Aristotle wrote about first principles more than two thousand years ago.

Thinking about thinking

Metacognition

Where it comes from: psychology. John Flavell gave it its name in 1979. It is why a good professional will say “I’m not sure about that.”

Standing on half a century of cognitive science.

  1. 1970sACT-R

    John R. Anderson at Carnegie Mellon separates what we know (facts) from what we can do (skills).

  2. 1980sSoar

    Allen Newell and colleagues build a unified model of how people solve problems.

  3. 2000sLIDA

    Stan Franklin at the University of Memphis models conscious attention and how it chooses what to do next.

  4. 2026Mahanta OS

    Brings these lines of research together in one operating layer on your own computer.

The layer that ties them together

Mahanta OS is what makes the three work as one.

It decides when each one is used, and it holds one rule above them all: nothing counts as done until it has been checked. Any one of these ideas makes an AI better. All three, working together, are what make BlueSpark™ something you can trust with your work.

Why you can trust it

The AI suggests. BlueSpark™ decides.

Every AI can sound confident. BlueSpark™ has to prove it.

The language model

Brings the ideas.

It writes the plan, the answer and the draft. Every one of them is a suggestion.

BlueSpark™'s checking system

Makes the call.

It checks every suggestion against your actual files. Nothing happens unless BlueSpark™ approves it.

01

Propose.

The AI suggests an action or an answer, clearly marked as a proposal.

02

Verify.

The claim is tested against the real world. What can’t be checked is labelled unverified and treated as not done.

03

Record.

Only verified results update memory and skills. The rest is kept honestly, labelled, and out of the way of future decisions.

Nothing counts until it’s checked.

When the AI says a job is done, BlueSpark™ doesn’t take its word for it. It checks the real result: the file exists, the number matches your document, the task actually happened.

It keeps a record.

Every step is written down before it happens. Nothing gets done twice by accident, and you can always see who did what, and why.

It knows when to stop.

If BlueSpark™ can’t confirm something, it doesn’t guess. It stops, tells you what it couldn’t check, and suggests what to do next.

It doesn’t hallucinate into your memory.

Anything unproven is kept out of what BlueSpark™ learns, so one bad guess never becomes a permanent “fact.”

Your files stay home.

Your documents, memory and history live on your own machine. No big IT project, no expensive consultants.

Your history opens like a local file.

The built-in conscience

The habit of double-checking before hitting send.

Every professional knows the feeling right before sending an important contract: a quiet pause, and an inner voice saying, “Wait. Did you check that tax schedule in paragraph 4?”

BlueSpark™ has that same pause built in. Before it saves a file, sends an update or confirms a number, it checks the real file on your hard drive. If a number doesn’t match, it stops. It never guesses and never fakes success.

The execution

Eleven capabilities, driven by curiosity.

Curiosity, memory and metacognition together give you eleven real capabilities on your Windows desktop. It answers in writing or out loud, with citations whenever it used your documents.

01

Checks real files

Never takes an AI’s word for it. It opens the real file, checks the numbers, and confirms the file exists before it says “done”.

02

Thinks when it counts

Quick answers for quick questions. It takes its time and deliberates when it is auditing an 80-page contract.

03

Admits when unsure

It knows what it knows and what it doesn’t. When it isn’t sure, it stops and asks you instead of making something up.

04

Fast daily habits

Show it how you like your monthly report formatted, and it remembers the habit and does it for you next time.

05

Drops old routines

If your folders or software change, it notices straight away and learns the new way.

06

Protects private notes

Casual chat, jokes and unverified rumours are kept in quarantine and never overwrite your permanent company rules.

07

Clear paper trail

A clear record of every document opened, every calculation made and every decision logged.

08

Works in Word and Excel

It doesn’t just give advice in a browser. It opens spreadsheets, reads PDFs, organises folders and writes drafts right on your PC. Type to it, or talk to it.

09

Catches mistakes before they run

Every command is checked for errors before it runs, so broken instructions are caught early.

10

Organised like your desk

Finds the exact note or contract you need across all five memory layers, without mixing up last year’s client with today’s.

11

You own everything

Your memory, habits and records live on your computer and belong to you.
